title: Handling money; the $5,000 first check
summary: She gave money to her husband and brother, got $5,000 for "Shorty George" and "Up the Country", and fought to get her share from her brother.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, that makes you feel independent, doesn't it, when you get the checks?
Oh, yeah, uh-huh.
You like that feeling of being an independent woman?
Well, I ain't no (unintelligible) for nothing.
Well, all the time when you were working and making records and singing, were you handling your own money or would you give it to the men you were with?
Husband, give it to him.
You gave it to him? You didn't handle your own money?

I didn't handle it. (Unintelligible) brother, I had a husband, but I give the money to my brother. When I got my first check home for "Shorty George," (unintelligible) "Shorty George" and "Up the Country." I don't know what Buddy got, but they said (unintelligible).
Yes, ma'am.
The first check?
The first check.
How come that was so much money?
(Unintelligible) record and said that
was the first colored record that had ever been sold, blues.
Yes, right.
And said, "Sippie, (unintelligible) -- and I sold more than Smith.
Oh, my.
Yes, sir.
$5,000.00. That's a lot of royalty for a record.

And then my brother -- now my brother hadn't -- so Miss ______, she was the secretary up there for the Okay Company. So they (unintelligible) give him the money. So at that time, my brother had to give me money. I didn't know. That ______ mad at my brother. Now, he knew ______ good as I was to him, he shouldn't have took no money from me. He should (unintelligible) singing, you know. And so I told Miss (unintelligible). Then I wrote my brother a letter and told him, I said, "You haven't ______ give you my money."
(Laughter.)
I say, "If you don't send me my money, I'm going to take other steps." I didn't know what steps meant. I said, "If you don't give me my money, I'm going to take other steps."
(Laughter.)
Now, I didn't know what that meant. I say, "I'm going to take other steps." My brother sent me $500.00.
